record.question:
An organization requires every production FSx for Windows File Server deployment to have managed availability across two Availability Zones. Some file systems are Single-AZ and receive frequent writes. A full restore would exceed the allowed write-outage window, but testing shows the remaining changes can be copied and verified during a short final freeze.

Which migration plan meets the policy with the least disruption?

options.text: Create a Multi-AZ file system, use DataSync for an initial copy and repeated incremental tasks while the source remains active, then freeze writes for a final verified transfer and switch clients.
Take one backup while the source remains writable, use the console restore wizard to change its deployment type to Multi-AZ, and switch clients later without transferring post-backup writes.
Create a second Single-AZ file system in another AZ, schedule DataSync copies, and manually switch clients if the original file system fails.
Edit the existing Single-AZ file system's deployment type to Multi-AZ in place, retaining its existing file-system identifier.

explanation.text:
<<1>> is correct. Copying most data before cutover limits the final outage to the remaining transfer, verification and client switch. The destination is an actual Multi-AZ FSx deployment with managed cross-AZ availability.

<<2>> attempts to change a deployment type that the documented console restore wizard fixes. It also omits writes made after the backup. <<3>> leaves two Single-AZ deployments and relies on scheduled copies and manual recovery, which does not meet the policy. <<4>> proposes an unsupported in-place deployment-type change.

DataSync executes transfer tasks; it is not continuous synchronous replication. Monitor incremental runs, keep one authoritative writer, and test the final copy and client reconnection. A backup protects a point in time; it does not by itself provide a continuously available, current Multi-AZ destination.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/migrate-files-to-fsx-datasync.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/high-availability-multiAZ.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateFileSystemWindowsConfiguration.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/datasync-large-migration-running-tasks.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/how-to-restore-backups.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-properties-fsx-filesystem-windowsconfiguration.html

diagram_alt: Repeated copies reduce the final delta, but safe migration still requires a write freeze, validation and an explicit client switch.

sources.supports: DataSync migrates on-premises files or files between FSx systems, including migration from Single-AZ to a new Multi-AZ file system.
Multi-AZ FSx for Windows uses a standby in another AZ and managed failover.
The Windows file-system update configuration does not expose a deployment-type conversion.
DataSync migration uses discrete initial and incremental tasks and a controlled final cutover.
The documented FSx Windows console backup-restore wizard has a fixed deployment type.
Changing FSx Windows DeploymentType requires replacement, not an in-place update.

editorial_notes: Repaired the continuous-DataSync claim and made later writes plus the outage constraint distinguish a one-time backup restore.
Corrected the inherited assertion that the console restore path can change Single-AZ backups to Multi-AZ; the current guide fixes deployment type. No broader API behavior is asserted.
